About

I lead the Secure and Trustworthy Intelligent Systems (SHIELD) Lab at SIU Carbondale. My research examines how intelligent systems can be made secure, privacy-preserving, and trustworthy.

My work focuses on secure, resource-efficient AI, usable privacy in generative AI systems, and forensics for AI-generated or AI-edited content. I also study how to make wearable and cyber-physical systems more secure and reliable, and how to bring responsible AI into computing education.

My affiliation with The ARCH, SIU’s Center for Advanced Research in Computational Humanities, brings humanities perspectives into my work on trustworthy AI and human-centered computing. I’m interested in what AI systems can infer or reveal when people write, speak, or create with them, including in immersive environments.

Research Interests

  • Secure and resource-efficient AI
  • Usable security and privacy for generative AI
  • Generative AI forensics
  • Adversarial and privacy-preserving machine learning
  • Wearable AI and cyber-physical systems
